item.title: Deterministic Genomic Integrity and Minimum Viable Population Topology in Deep-Space Mars Colonization: Mitigating Founder Bottlenecks, Cosmic-Ray Mutational Meltdown, and Hereditary Disease Risk via QFS-zkVM and Human-in-Command (HIC) Bio-Sovereignty
item.description:
[预印本] Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
Maintenance of genetic diversity is an absolute biological prerequisite for the multi-generational survival of any isolated human population. In the context of long-duration Mars exploration and permanent extra-terrestrial settlement, extreme founder bottlenecks (low effective population size $N_e$), restricted gene flow from Earth, and chronic exposure to Galactic Cosmic Radiation (GCR) and Solar Particle Events (SPE) synergistically accelerate loss of heterozygosity ($H_t$), inbreeding depression ($F_t$), and the expression of deleterious autosomal recessive disorders. Left ungoverned, finite habitats face irreversible mutational meltdown via Muller's Ratchet. Conversely, delegating demographic and reproductive risk management to opaque, probabilistic artificial intelligence introduces severe bio-ethical hazards, including algorithmic eugenics and coercion. This monograph establishes a rigorous population-genetic, thermodynamic, and cryptographic framework for Martian genomic resilience. First, we formalize coupled drift-radiation decay equations under Reality-Thermodynamic Optimization (RTO P2.0), deriving exact minimum viable effective population thresholds ($N_e^*$) and synthetic allele-infusion schedules using shielded cryogenic germplasm repositories. Second, we architect a privacy-preserving, deterministic genomic compatibility and somatic mutation auditing engine over the 64-bit Goldilocks prime field ($\mathbb{F}_p, p = 2^{64} - 2^{32} + 1$) inside the Quantum Financial & Infrastructure System Zero-Knowledge Virtual Machine (QFS-zkVM) paired with Q-SAFA hardware telemetry. Third, we codify constitutional and statutory safeguards anchored in Human-in-Command (HIC) bio-sovereignty, the 1967 Outer Space Treaty, fiduciary oversight under Delaware Caremark doctrine, and pre-execution risk gates analogous to SEC Rule 15c3-5. 【日本語要旨】深宇宙・火星探査における決定論的ゲノム完全性と最小存続可能個体群(MVP)トポロジー:創始者ボトルネック、宇宙線変異メルトダウン、および遺伝的疾患リスクのQFS-zkVM・人間主権(HIC)による抑制モデル。Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) with Strict No-Learn Covenant (NLL-v1.0-2026).

item.title: When Does Nature Become Therapy? Reconsidering Therapeutic Experience, Agency, Professional Guidance, and Commercialisation in Shinrin-Yoku, Forest Bathing and Forest Therapy
item.description:
Shinrin-Yoku Journal
The term therapy is increasingly employed across practices concerned with human well-being, including music therapy, sound therapy, aromatherapy, nature therapy, forest therapy, and Shinrin-Yoku. However, its meaning varies considerably across clinical, scientific, cultural, professional, and commercial contexts. An experience may be perceived as therapeutic without constituting a formal therapeutic intervention, just as a service may be marketed as therapy without possessing an established clinical methodology or clearly demonstrated therapeutic efficacy. This article critically examines the meaning and implications of therapy within forest-based practices. Drawing on research in environmental psychology, public health, forest medicine, sociology, nature connectedness, and therapeutic relationships, alongside Japanese historical developments and the author’s previous conceptual work, the discussion questions where therapeutic agency resides. Is it the forest environment, the guide, the participant, the social context, or the interactions among these elements that make an experience therapeutic? The analysis distinguishes between therapeutic effects, therapeutic intentions, organised well-being interventions, and clinically delivered treatments. It further considers the evolution of Shinrin-Yoku into contemporary forest therapy terminology, the value and limitations of professional guidance, relational approaches to forest engagement, and the commercialisation of nature-based experiences. Particular attention is given to the possibility that meaningful and restorative experiences can emerge through ordinary, unstructured contact with nature, without professional guidance or explicit therapeutic intention. The article proposes a relational and context-sensitive understanding of therapeutic experience, supported by principles of co-creation, co-responsibility, and co-being. Rather than seeking a universal definition of forest therapy, the discussion advocates greater conceptual precision, professional transparency, methodological pluralism, and critical reflection. It concludes that the therapeutic potential of an experience cannot be adequately determined by its name, setting, or professional structure alone. Keywords: Shinrin-Yoku; forest bathing; forest therapy; nature therapy; therapeutic experience; nature-based interventions; therapeutic agency; forest therapy guides; relational well-being; commercialisation; medicalisation; nature connectedness

item.title: Handcrafted Feature Extraction and Classification for Distinguishing Real and AI-Generated Images
item.description:
The Journal of Applied Technology and Innovation
The generative machine-learning approaches are extensively used to create artificial images. These images are called AI-generated images. The AI-generated images find applications like rapid content creation, creative design and visualization, rapid prototyping, etc. In spite of many applications, the AI-generated images are leading to issues like bias, copyright issues, deepfakes, etc. Owing to the importance of discriminating between synthetic and real images, many research approaches have been proposed. Among these methods, deep learning approaches are popular. However, the design of common deep learning detection approaches to detect the synthetic images that are generated by different generative models is a challenging task. There are issues with these methods to discriminate images that are subjected to various pre-processing steps. To overcome these issues, machine learning approaches with the handcrafted features are gaining importance. In this context, five types of handcrafted feature extraction and random forest-based classification is proposed to distinguish between AI-generated and real images. The simulation experiments are carried out with AI-generated and real facial images, with each group having 70,000 samples. Out of 70,000 samples from each group, 50,000, 10,000, and 10,000 samples are respectively used for training, validating, and testing the classifier. The performance of the classifier is evaluated for accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score. The recognition accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 scores of 86.03%, 86.15%, 85.87%, and 86.01%, respectively, are achieved for three feature combinations

item.title: Overview of the Current State and Prospects of Artificial Intelligence
item.description:
Journal of Research in Engineering and Computer Sciences
Between 2023 and 2026, artificial intelligence (AI) reached a decisive stage of development. From language models capable of logical reasoning to autonomous agents able to carry out complex tasks, AI is redefining the boundaries of productivity, creativity, and employment. This review provides a broad overview of AI in 2026, covering its core technologies, major market participants, practical impacts, and ethical challenges, while examining the current state of the field and its likely future direction.

item.title: La “creatività” dell’IA e le sue proprietà: definizioni e criticità nell’era dei LLM
item.description:
AI-Linguistica Linguistic Studies on AI-Generated Texts and Discourses
Il concetto di “creatività”, virtù spesso attribuita all’intelletto o alla fantasia dell’essere umano, è di recente divenuto oggetto di trattazione all’interno di testi scientifici sull’IA. Per tale motivo, diversi ambiti di ricerca si preoccupano di definire una nuova ontologia della creatività che prenda in considerazione la continua evoluzione di sistemi artificiali come i LLM. In linea con tali sviluppi, la presente ricerca propone una definizione critica della creatività nell’ambito dell’IA, basata sui cinque elementi fondamentali della creatività: agente (actor), processo (process), prodotto (outcome), dominio (domain) e spazio (space). Una successiva analisi quantitativo-qualitativa basata su corpus riflette poi sugli usi linguistici dell’aggettivo creative in testi di computer science ad alto rigore scientifico e sulla sua co-occorrenza in relazione a termini riguardanti i cinque elementi fondamentali, classificati secondo la ricerca di Wingström et al. (2022).

item.title: Transformative learning in farmer research networks: insights from Eastern and Southern Africa
item.description:
[预印本] Figshare
Farmer research networks are collaborative platforms where farmers, researchers, extension workers, and NGOs co-create knowledge, experiment with innovations, and tackle local challenges through joint learning and action. Although interest in these networks is growing, there remains a limited understanding of how learning occurs within them. This study draws on qualitative data from nine networks active between 2015 and 2024 in Kenya, Malawi and Uganda. It reveals that these networks foster individual and collective transformation. The process is dynamic, multi-dimensional, technical, relational, and emotional, shaped by diverse knowledge systems and social interactions. Emotional engagement , enhanced motivation, deepened reflection, and prompted identity shifts. Networks function not only as sites of knowledge co-creation and learning but also as cultural and emotional spaces where agricultural visions and identities are negotiated and reshaped. Farmers assumed roles as researchers and educators, adapting agroecological innovations and experimenting with solutions to ecological and livelihood challenges. The key enabling factors were trust among members, inclusive facilitation, institutional memory, and strong local leadership. Progress was constrained by entrenched gender norms, hierarchical extension practices, and rigid social structures. Sustaining transformative learning calls for continued investment in facilitation capacity, inclusive leadership and institutional structures that embed networks within broader innovation systems.

item.title: Problem analysis of curriculum development for application-oriented undergraduate art and design programs in Chinese-foreign cooperative education: a case study
item.description:
Forum for education studies.
Based on the OBE (Outcome-Based Education) philosophy, this study examines the construction of curriculum systems for application-oriented undergraduate art and design programs in Chinese-foreign cooperative education, taking the Modern International Art & Design Academy of Chongqing Technology and Business University as a case study. The research identifies four core challenges in practice at present: a gap between application-oriented talent cultivation goals and OBE principles; an incomplete curriculum system that integrates local needs with an international perspective; a dual-standard issue in assessment and evaluation systems oriented toward students’ long-term career development; and the absence of an effective collaborative mechanism between Chinese and foreign faculty despite their physical co-presence. These problems essentially reflect the structural tension between internationalization and localization. The study proposes that the solution lies in constructing a new educational logic of integrated co-creation, applying an outcome-oriented approach throughout the entire process of goal setting, curriculum reconstruction, evaluation reform, and faculty development. This approach would promote the organic integration of international design education resources with local industry-education collaboration, and establish a career competency tracking and support system that runs through the entire cultivation process. This study also provides a problem definition and analytical framework for similar institutions seeking to advance high-quality development in Chinese-foreign cooperative education.

item.title: ЛАКУНАРНОСТЬ В ХУДОЖЕСТВЕННОМ ТЕКСТЕ: ЭКСПЛИЦИТНЫЕ И ИМПЛИЦИТНЫЕ АСПЕКТЫ
item.description:
Вестник Адыгейского государственного университета серия «Филология и искусствоведение»
В статье рассматривается феномен лакунарности как фундаментального принципа организации художественного текста, обеспечивающего его смысловую глубину и эстетическую ценность. Анализируются два взаимосвязанных аспекта лакунарности: эксплицитный, связанный со структурными пропусками в повествовании (композиционные разрывы, диалогические паузы, темпоральные скачки, синтаксические эллипсисы), и имплицитный, отвечающий за генерацию скрытых смыслов (психологический, идейно-философский и культурно-аксиологический подтекст). На материале романа У. Теккерея «Ярмарка тщеславия» демонстрируется, что взаимодействие выраженного и невыраженного активизирует читательское восприятие, превращая чтение в процесс сотворчества. Доказывается, что лакунарность является не случайным элементом, а строго организованной системой, повышающей интерпретационный потенциал текста и обеспечивающей его многозначность. The article examines the phenomenon of lacunarity as a fundamental principle of the organization of a literary text, ensuring its semantic depth and aesthetic value. Two interrelated aspects of lacunarity are analyzed: the explicit one, associated with structural gaps in the narrative (compositional breaks, dialogical pauses, temporal jumps, syntactic ellipses), and the implicit one, responsible for generating hidden meanings (psychological, ideological, philosophical, and cultural-axiological overtones). Based on the novel by U. Thackeray «Vanity Fair» it demonstrates that the interaction of the expressed and the unexpressed activates the reader's perception, turning reading into a process of co-creation. It is proved that lacunarity is not an accidental element, but a strictly organized system that increases the interpretative potential of the text and ensures its ambiguity.

Avant de dire ce qu'un instrument détecte, il faut savoir ce qu'il mesure lorsque rien ne change volontairement. Ce silence expérimental permet d'estimer le bruit et de fixer un seuil de détection. Mais certaines transformations restent invisibles à une représentation, même en l'absence de bruit. Il ne démontre pas encore une anticipation de défaillance, une supériorité prédictive ou une efficacité opérationnelle. Un protocole de confrontation avec les indicateurs classiques de tension, pente, courbure, amplitude et capacité est fourni, mais n'a pas encore été exécuté sur les batteries réelles. This experimental silence helps estimate noise and establish detection thresholds. Yet some transformations remain invisible to a representation even in the absence of noise. COS45 provides an explicit mathematical construction based on time series, sliding windows, Hankel matrices, spectral decomposition, projectors, and trajectories on a Grassmannian. item.title: Two-Stage Non-Equilibrium Oncogenomic Drift, Lyso-GL1 Clonal Hazard, and Deterministic Hardware Interlocks (PHOENIX_ROUTER & NLL-v1.0-2026): Unifying 1q21 GBA1 B-Cell Malignancies, Archipelagic XPA/FANC Recessive Syndromes, and TP53/BRCA Thermodynamic Unfolding Across the Pediatric–AYA Statutory Cliff

Treatises I through IV established a mathematically rigorous synthesis linking 1q21 GBA1/GBAP1 non-allelic homologous recombination (NAHR), the 101.5x hierarchical Wahlund amplification observed in Japan's N=90 Gaucher disease cohort, tripartite archipelagic ancestral stratification (K1 Jomon, K2 Yayoi, K3 Kofun) under post-industrial rural depopulation (gamma_d > 0), and sub-500-nanosecond hardware governance via PHOENIX_ROUTER over the 64-bit Goldilocks prime field F_p (p = 2^64 - 2^32 + 1). In this fifth monograph (Treatise V), we extend this deterministic framework directly into molecular oncology, pediatric/adolescent and young adult (AYA) hereditary cancer predisposition, and clinical genomic data sovereignty. First, we formulate a two-stage non-equilibrium stochastic differential and point-process framework across three oncogenomic pillars: (i) Pillar I: 1q21 GBA1 L444P/RecNciI germline drift (Gamma = 101.5x) coupled to glucosylsphingosine (Lyso-GL1) lipid-antigen accumulation driven by Gibbs unfolding perturbation (DeltaDeltaG_fold = +4.8 +/- 0.4 kcal/mol), which triggers CD1d-restricted Type II NKT activation and accelerates somatic clonal hazard from monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance (MGUS) to multiple myeloma and B-cell lymphoma; (ii) Pillar II: autosomal recessive DNA-repair founder syndromes amplified by Yayoi-Kofun bottlenecks and regional deme contraction, exemplified by 9q22.3 XPA (IVS3-1G>C splice founder variant, carrier frequency ~1%) in xeroderma pigmentosum group A and FANCA/FANCG in Fanconi anemia; and (iii) Pillar III: Knudson two-hit tumor suppressor inactivation and core domain melting in 17p13.1 TP53 (Li-Fraumeni syndrome) and BRCA1/BRCA2 (biallelic Fanconi subtypes D1/S and monoallelic AYA breast, ovarian, and CNS malignancies). Second, we introduce a Lifetime Cumulative Treatment Burden and Late-Effects Free-Energy Tensor T_late(a) capturing irreversible anthracycline cardiotoxicity and radiotherapy tissue damage (d||T_late(a)||_F / da >= 0). Third, we formalize the Statutory Drop-Off Interlock within PHOENIX_ROUTER to physically ground (WE_STATE_ROOT = 0 V in < 500 ns) administrative subsidy termination when pediatric cancer survivors are structurally omitted from Japan's adult Designated Intractable Disease schedule at age a_0 in {18, 20} (Delta S(a_0) = S_pediatric). Finally, we expand the Strict No-Learn Covenant Hardware Firewall (NLL-v1.0-2026) with a unidirectional DMA optical data diode and 2-clock-cycle (RTO P2.0, < 4.0 ns) register zeroization circuit that physically blocks unauthorized gradient backpropagation and exfiltration of patient Comprehensive Genomic Profiling (CGP) germline and somatic variant tensors by external AI platforms. item.title: Parallax · Twin Tales No. 11 — Call for Help: Off · The Howl
item.description:
[预印本] Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
A pair of short stories from Parallax · Twin Tales, which stage one real dilemma twice: Here, in the world as it is, with invented people in real places; There, in the world of Vision Come True, a future that split from ours in 2024 and never emerged. This pair belongs with the eighteenth essay of Brainstorming with the Enemy, The Gauge and the Mute, and adds what the essay leaves out: the people who love us, and want to do the muting for us. Both tales are pages from a notebook, written by hand by an old pharmacist after a night he needs to understand. Here, in Vélez-Málaga in November 2026, two weeks before Spain votes, Rafael Ortega, born under Franco and widowed in the spring, writes to his late wife. His daughter has set up two machines to protect him: a shared set of rules that mutes the town council's notice that the tap water is unfit to drink, and a ring that reports to her, with its call for help switched off. When he falls in the night, the ring tells only her, and her phone is on silent. He writes his way from anger to its cause, names the fear rather than the daughter, and gives her back a smaller, truer part. There, on the shore of the Seventh Lake in 2059, Faris Nasrallah, born in Haifa in 1985, lives with the inward hum of his body and the outward hum of his shore, his mutes his own and dated, his daughter's calls landing at a volume he sets. One night the honest instruments of the whole shore begin to howl, as bodies react to the very hum they feed; he mutes it for an hour, tests the reaction the way a pharmacist tests a drug, and has the echoes counted once, and in his notebook asks what is still left to tune. Written in part with Claude (Anthropic), an AI model. The ideas, editorial decisions and responsibility for the content are the author's.

item.title: Brainstorming with the Enemy No. 18 — The Gauge and the Mute
item.description:
[预印本] Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
The eighteenth essay in Brainstorming with the Enemy began with a question typed before the author was properly awake, on 23 October 2026: his news reaches him through Google News and YouTube, and the watch that counts his lengths in the pool also counts his heartbeats at night, so how should he read, filter, own, set, keep, keep safe and share what they know? The argument with an AI that followed is told as it happened: the questions and objections are the author's, and the facts and studies are presented as the machine's input. The seven verbs sort themselves into twin machines: a news dashboard that reads the world for its owner, and a health dashboard that reads its owner. The essay draws one line through both. An owner may mute what he would rather not see, as medicine came to accept with the right not to be told; nobody may move the needle on the gauge, reporting a reading as more or less certain than the evidence allows. It shows that the twins are threatened from opposite directions, the news by text written to move the reading, the body by a record that leaks out; that the hardest settings are made by those who love us, through the care idea of the dignity of risk; and that the readings of many bodies form a shared hum that should share the answer, never the itinerary. It proposes five ideas to try: mute freely and leave the gauge alone; count the mutes for the owner only; give every mute an end date; keep the twins apart, their settings private, and call help before family; and leave one bell for danger to life beneath both. It leaves three questions open for readers to work on with their own AI, makes three requests, to the makers of assistants and wearables, to the authorities for medical devices and data, and to Switzerland's public-alert office, and gives, as an addendum, the Mute Ledger, with three measures and four predictions and what would refute each. Concepts proposed by the author: the Gauge and the Mute; the Mute Ledger. Written in part with Claude (Anthropic), an AI model. The ideas, editorial decisions and responsibility for the content are the author's.

item.title: Education Attack
item.description:
[预印本] Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
Artificial intelligence (AI), generative artificial intelligence (GenAI), large language models (LLMs), autonomous agents, robotics, and embodied intelligence are transforming the capabilities available to students, teachers, and educational institutions. These technologies can improve access to information, personalize instruction, automate routine tasks, and support educational creativity. However, they also introduce a broader class of risks that cannot be fully characterized by conventional cybersecurity, academic integrity, or educational technology frameworks. Students may obtain answers without engaging in the reasoning that assignments are intended to develop. Teachers may generate lesson plans, explanations, assessments, and instructional materials without undertaking the corresponding intellectual work. Autonomous agents and embodied systems may further extend such substitution from producing digital content to executing educational tasks in digital and physical environments. This paper introduces Education Attack as a proposed conceptual framework for analyzing how technological capabilities can bypass, substitute for, manipulate, or weaken the processes through which education is intended to produce learning and teaching outcomes. Unlike conventional cyberattacks, which typically target the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of information systems, Education Attack focuses on the integrity and effectiveness of educational functions. The framework distinguishes learner-process attacks, teaching-process attacks, assessment attacks, agency-substitution attacks, and system-level educational attacks. It defines a threat model, proposes a formal representation of educational functional degradation, identifies potential attack pathways, and develops a preliminary taxonomy of risks associated with AI-enabled educational environments. It also outlines corresponding defensive strategies, including process-aware assessment, human capability verification, transparent delegation, and education-centered security evaluation. This paper is conceptual and does not claim empirical validation of the proposed framework. Its central proposition is that educational systems require a broader security perspective that examines not only whether technologies function correctly, but also whether their use preserves the educational functions those technologies are intended to support.

item.title: Reproducibility package: The missing parameter — an agent-based study of cost, attention and the coexistence of AI-generated and human-created dance
item.description:
[预印本] Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
Reproducibility package for the manuscript "The missing parameter: an agent-based study of cost, attention and the coexistence of AI-generated and human-created dance" (Digital Creativity).
